patterns: send someone on a wild-goose chase
lead someone on a wild-goose chase
prove to be a wild-goose chase
end up being a wild-goose chase
nothing more than a wild-goose chase

usage.meaning: A wild-goose chase is a complicated, confused, or lengthy search that is unlikely to succeed.
usage.article: As a singular countable noun phrase, it normally takes an article: a wild-goose chase or the wild-goose chase.
usage.verbs: Common verbs include go on, send, lead, turn into, and prove to be.
usage.hyphenation: Wild-goose is traditionally hyphenated in the noun phrase, although wild goose chase without hyphens is also common. When the entire phrase modifies another noun, wild-goose-chase may be fully hyphenated.
usage.evaluation: The expression implies that time and effort have been wasted because the goal was unattainable, nonexistent, incorrectly identified, or pursued on the basis of misleading information.
usage.register: It is idiomatic and natural in conversation, journalism, and moderately informal professional writing.

ja: 成果が得られる見込みのない、無駄な捜索・追跡
誤った情報や手掛かりに基づいて行われる見当違いの調査
対象が存在しない、または見つけられないため徒労に終わる試み
複雑で長時間を要するにもかかわらず、目的を達成できない探索
人を混乱させ、時間や労力を浪費させる一連の行動
en: a search or pursuit that has little or no chance of producing a useful result
a misguided investigation based on false information or an incorrect clue
an attempt that proves futile because its object does not exist or cannot be found
a complicated and lengthy search that fails to achieve its purpose
a sequence of actions that causes confusion and wastes time or effort

nuance.ja: a wild-goose chase は、単に捜索が難しいというだけでなく、最初から手掛かりが誤っていたり、対象が存在しなかったりして、費やした時間や労力が結局無駄になることを強調する。go on a wild-goose chase は自分が無駄な捜索に出ること、send someone on a wild-goose chase は誤情報などによって人を無駄足にさせることを表す。後者には、意図的に相手を惑わせたという含みが生じることもある。ただし、結果的に当てが外れただけの場合にも使えるため、必ずしも欺く意図を意味しない。調査・書類探し・技術的な原因究明など、物理的な追跡以外にも広く使われる。
nuance.en: A wild-goose chase emphasizes more than the difficulty of a search. It suggests that the time and effort were ultimately wasted because the original clue was wrong, the objective did not exist, or the search was fundamentally misdirected. Go on a wild-goose chase describes undertaking such a search, while send someone on a wild-goose chase means causing another person to pursue a useless lead. The latter can imply deliberate deception, but it may also describe an innocent mistake that sends someone in the wrong direction. The idiom applies broadly to investigations, searches for documents, troubleshooting, and other unsuccessful efforts as well as literal pursuit.

ja: a wild-goose chase：誤った手掛かりなどによる、成果の見込めない無駄な捜索・追跡。
fruitless search：努力しても成果を得られない捜索。比喩性の低い中立的な表現。
futile pursuit：成功の見込みがない追求・追跡。やや形式的。
dead end：それ以上進展できない行き止まりの手掛かり・方針。
red herring：重要な問題から注意をそらす、無関係または誤解を招く情報。
fool’s errand：成功する見込みがなく、引き受けること自体が愚かな仕事。
runaround：責任回避などによって、人をあちこちへ行かせる不誠実な対応。
goose chase：wild-goose chase を短縮した口語的な形だが、完全な表現の方が一般的。
en: a wild-goose chase is a useless or misdirected search, often caused by an incorrect clue.
a fruitless search is a search that produces no result and is comparatively neutral and literal.
a futile pursuit is a somewhat formal term for an attempt or pursuit with no realistic prospect of success.
a dead end is a clue, approach, or situation from which no further progress can be made.
a red herring is irrelevant or misleading information that diverts attention from the real issue.
a fool’s errand is a task whose lack of any realistic chance of success makes undertaking it foolish.
the runaround is evasive treatment that sends someone between people or places without resolving the matter.
goose chase is an informal shortened form, although the complete expression wild-goose chase is more established.

etymology.ja: wild-goose chase は、もともと野生のガンを実際に追いかけることではなく、先頭の騎手が選んだ不規則な進路を、後続の騎手が一定の間隔を置いて追う競技を指したと考えられている。その隊形が飛行するガンの群れに似ていたことが名称の由来とされる。シェイクスピアの『ロミオとジュリエット』には、機知の応酬をこの競技にたとえた初期の比喩的用例が見られる。競技そのものが忘れられるにつれて、表現は捕まえにくい野生のガンを追い回すイメージと結び付けて理解されるようになり、現在の「成果の見込めない無駄な捜索」という意味が定着した。
etymology.en: Wild-goose chase is generally understood to have originally named a form of horseback sport rather than the literal pursuit of a wild bird. In the sport, following riders reportedly had to reproduce the irregular course taken by a leading rider at set intervals, creating a formation compared to a flight of geese. An early figurative use appears in Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet, where a contest of wit is compared to such a chase. As knowledge of the sport faded, the expression was reinterpreted through the image of unsuccessfully pursuing a difficult-to-catch wild goose, and its modern sense of a futile or misdirected search became established.

note.ja: 努力したにもかかわらず、目的の物・情報・人物を発見できない捜索。
note.en: A search that fails to locate the desired object, information, or person despite the effort made.

note.ja: 成功の可能性がほとんどなく、行うこと自体が愚かに見える仕事・任務。
note.en: A task or mission with so little chance of success that undertaking it appears foolish.

note.ja: 目的を達成できる現実的な見込みがない追求・試み。
note.en: A pursuit or attempt with no realistic prospect of achieving its objective.

note.ja: 調査や問題解決において、それ以上の進展につながらない手掛かり・方針。
note.en: A clue or approach that provides no opportunity for further progress in an investigation or problem.

note.ja: 本当の問題・容疑者・論点から注意をそらす、無関係または誤解を招くもの。
note.en: Something irrelevant or misleading that diverts attention from the real issue, suspect, or argument.

ja: The incorrect address sent us on a wild-goose chase across the city. — 間違った住所のせいで、私たちは市内をあちこち無駄に探し回ることになった。
We spent hours looking for a document that had never existed, so the search was a complete wild-goose chase. — 私たちは最初から存在しなかった文書を何時間も探し、捜索は完全な徒労に終わった。
His vague instructions led the technical team on a wild-goose chase. — 彼の曖昧な指示によって、技術チームは見当違いの原因究明をすることになった。
Please confirm the serial number before starting the investigation so that we do not go on a wild-goose chase. — 無駄な調査を始めずに済むよう、調査開始前にシリアル番号を確認してください。
The patent attorney checked the publication number first to avoid sending the search team on a wild-goose chase through unrelated prior art. — 弁理士は、調査チームが無関係な先行技術を無駄に探し回らないよう、最初に公開番号を確認した。
en: The incorrect address sent us on a wild-goose chase across the city.
We spent hours looking for a document that had never existed, so the search was a complete wild-goose chase.
His vague instructions led the technical team on a wild-goose chase.
Please confirm the serial number before starting the investigation so that we do not go on a wild-goose chase.
The patent attorney checked the publication number first to avoid sending the search team on a wild-goose chase through unrelated prior art.

patterns: dismiss someone as a one-trick pony
prove someone is not a one-trick pony
a company that is a one-trick pony

usage.person: A one-trick pony is a person who is known for only one skill, talent, method, or successful idea.
usage.thing: The expression can also describe a company, product, technology, or strategy that performs only one useful function.
usage.article: As a singular countable noun, it normally requires an article or another determiner: a one-trick pony.
usage.plural: The plural is one-trick ponies, with pony changing to ponies.
usage.hyphenation: One-trick is hyphenated because it functions as a compound modifier of pony.
usage.evaluation: The expression is usually critical, but speakers may use it humorously or reject it by saying someone is more than a one-trick pony.
usage.strength: It does not necessarily deny excellence in the one area; it criticizes the lack of versatility.

ja: 一つの技能・芸・方法しか持っていない人
一つの分野でしか成功できないと見なされる人物
一つの機能・商品・戦略だけに依存している企業や製品
応用力・多様性・柔軟性に欠ける人または物
同じ手法や話題ばかりを繰り返す人物
en: a person who has only one notable skill, talent, or method
someone regarded as capable of succeeding in only one field
a company or product dependent on a single function, product, or strategy
a person or thing lacking versatility, variety, or flexibility
someone who repeatedly relies on the same technique or subject

nuance.ja: one-trick pony は、一つのことしかできない人・企業・製品を、芸を一つだけ覚えた小馬にたとえる表現である。その一つの能力が低いという意味ではなく、非常に優れていても、それ以外の能力や選択肢を持たないことを批判する。例えば、一つのヒット商品だけに収益を依存する会社や、一種類の役しか演じない俳優にも使える。通常は否定的だが、I’m not a one-trick pony. のように、自分には複数の能力があると主張する形でもよく使われる。
nuance.en: A one-trick pony is compared to a small performing horse trained to perform only one one routine. The expression does not necessarily suggest that the single ability is weak; the person or thing may be excellent at it. The criticism concerns the absence of versatility or alternative capabilities. It can describe an actor associated with one kind of role, a company dependent on one successful product, or technology serving only one purpose. The phrase is normally negative, but it is also common in statements such as I’m not a one-trick pony, which assert broader ability.

ja: one-trick pony：一つの能力・方法・商品・機能しか持たない人や物。
specialist：特定分野に深い知識・技能を持つ人。必ずしも否定的ではない。
versatile：多様な仕事・役割・用途に対応できる。
limited：能力・用途・範囲などが限られている。
one-dimensional：性格・作品・考え方などに深みや多様性がない。
one-hit wonder：一つの作品だけが大成功し、その後成功が続かなかった人・団体。
jack-of-all-trades：多くの異なる仕事・技能をこなせる人。
more than meets the eye：外見から分かる以上の能力・複雑さを持つ。
en: a one-trick pony is a person or thing possessing only one notable ability, method, product, or function.
a specialist has extensive knowledge or skill in one field and is not necessarily viewed negatively.
versatile describes someone or something capable of performing many different tasks or roles.
limited describes ability, usefulness, or scope that does not extend very far.
one-dimensional describes a personality, work, or idea lacking depth and variety.
a one-hit wonder is a performer or group successful for one work but unable to repeat that success.
a jack-of-all-trades is someone capable of performing many different kinds of work.
more than meets the eye describes someone or something with greater ability or complexity than initially apparent.

etymology.ja: one-trick pony は、見世物などで一つの芸だけを教えられた pony「小馬」のイメージから生まれたアメリカ英語の表現である。観客を一度は楽しませられても、同じ芸しかできなければ演目に多様性がない。そこから、一つの才能・方法・製品・機能だけに依存し、それ以外の場面では能力を発揮できない人・企業・物を比喩的に表すようになった。
etymology.en: One-trick pony developed in American English from the image of a small performing horse trained to execute only one trick. Such an animal might entertain an audience once but would offer no variety beyond that routine. The image consequently became a metaphor for a person, company, product, or method dependent on one talent, successful idea, or useful function and unable to demonstrate comparable ability elsewhere.

note.ja: 能力・性格・考え方・作品などに多様性や深みがない。
note.en: Lacking variety or depth in ability, personality, thought, or artistic treatment.

note.ja: 一つの作品・商品だけで大成功したものの、その成功を再現できなかった人・団体。
note.en: A person or group successful with one work or product but unable to repeat that success.

note.ja: 能力・用途・選択肢・適用範囲などが狭い。
note.en: Restricted in ability, usefulness, available options, or scope.

note.ja: 非常に限定された一分野・用途だけに特化している。
note.en: Concentrated on a very restricted field, activity, or function.

note.ja: 同じ方法・行動・内容を繰り返し、多様性に欠ける。
note.en: Repeatedly using the same method, action, or content and therefore lacking variety.

ja: Critics initially dismissed the actor as a one-trick pony. — 批評家たちは当初、その俳優を一種類の役しか演じられない人物として退けた。
The company cannot depend on one successful product forever, or it will become a one-trick pony. — その会社は一つのヒット商品へ永遠に依存することはできず、そうすれば一つのことしかできない企業になってしまう。
The software is useful, but it is something of a one-trick pony. — そのソフトウェアは便利だが、用途が一つに限られている。
Her second novel proved that she was not a one-trick pony. — 彼女の二作目の小説は、彼女が一つの作風しか持たない作家ではないことを証明した。
A patent covering only one narrow implementation may become a one-trick pony with limited commercial value. — 一つの限定的な実施形態だけを対象とする特許は、商業的価値の限られた一用途だけの権利になる可能性がある。
en: Critics initially dismissed the actor as a one-trick pony.

The software is useful, but it is something of a one-trick pony.
Her second novel proved that she was not a one-trick pony.
A patent covering only one narrow implementation may become a one-trick pony with limited commercial value.
